item.description: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) Defensively, the Las Vegas Raiders are trending up after holding the defending champion Seattle Seahawks to under 30 points and a respectable 21 points. Creating two turnovers, with the first being two plays into the first possession and the other deep inside the red zone. Can they keep up the good work against the division-leading Denver Broncos? It’s not impossible, but it will take a cohesive effort. The Broncos are winning games by scoring just enough. Defensively, they are allowing an average of 20.7 points per game, 9th-best. Yet on offense, they are averaging 22.0 points per game, which, ironically, is 22nd-best in the league. In contrast, the complementary football model that head coach Sean Payton is deploying in 2026 is working. Horses before the cart Bo Nix isn’t exactly lighting the world on fire with his play. His QBR ranking of 49.0 is ranked 23rd in the league and his 84.7 quarterback Rating is 21st. He’s passed for 1,730 yards (T-20th), completing a mere 60.6% of his passes (24th among starting quarterbacks), T-8th least yards per completion (6.0), and 17th in passing touchdowns (11). The 11 sacks are 16th in the league, and 57 sack yards are the lowest in the league for a starting quarterback. Shockingly, Nix’s rushing numbers are the lowest of his career; his 3.1 yards per carry are the lowest by over a yard. Despite having a huge 62-yard touchdown run to boost his numbers. The mighty Broncos rushing attack is hardly anything to write home about. Much like the Raiders, the Broncos’ rushing attack is by committee; no individual averages more than 40 yards per game. item.description: Credit: FS1, Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Fairly or unfairly, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter has developed a reputation for slanting his reporting in agents and players’ favor. Nick Wright of FS1’s First Things First would just like Schefter to report on New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye at all. Last Sunday, Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson sacked Maye during the first quarter of Detroit’s 35-10 win over New England in Munich, Germany. Maye exited the game and did not return, and Maye remained in Germany for further testing on his ankle for an indeterminate amount of time. First Things First , hosted by die-hard Patriots fan Kevin Wildes, has made the odd ambiguity around Maye’s injury into a bit this week. To be fair to Schefter, he and ESPN’s Mike Reiss finally reported the results of Maye’s tests by Friday afternoon. According to their joint report , Maye suffered a fractured right fibula but no additional ligament damage. The injury won’t require surgery, but his ability to play again this season is in serious doubt. But that came after Wright delivered a fair criticism during the show’s weekly “ Chris Broussard’s Under Duress List ” segment on Thursday. “Drake Maye played a football game in Germany early Sunday morning,” Wright said. “Yeah, do you have any updates?” Wildes quipped. “It’s Thursday afternoon,” Wright said. “It’s 4:09 Eastern. item.title: Jerry Jones makes curious surveillance claim amid Cowboys fan death investigation
item.description: News broke on Friday that 36-year-old Mario Narro died in the hospital several days after getting into a fight with a fan and then falling during the 49ers-Cowboys game . Cowboys owner Jerry Jones gave interesting comments about this during an appearance on “105.3 The Fan” on Friday. Jerry Jones of the Dallas Cowboys looks on prior to a game against the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images Jones was asked whether he was aware of the fight that resulted in the fan’s death and whether the Arlington Police Department contacted the Cowboys for video footage of what happened. “No record of any incidents at the game, and I just got that information. And so we had no record of an incident, and we’ll obviously be looking into that,” Jones said. “My understanding is the individual went to the game and didn’t feel good at the game, and then left, and has been hospitalized. But we weren’t aware of any incident that involved a fan at the game,” he added. “Let me make the point of, we really do have quite a — eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago — we have quite a surveillance of what’s going on at every aspect of our game. And so it is really rare if we didn’t know of any incident. We’ve got too many people out there; we have 6,000 workers on game day. Mario Narro posing in a Dallas Cowboys jersey. Narro died on Wednesday after injuries suffered from during a fight at a Dallas Cowboys game. “Of course!” Jones then said several times when asked whether they would provide any footage to the police if they asked for it. Jones likely just heard this story and does not have all the information. But his sentiment about the stadium’s surveillance is interesting, to say the least. AT&T Stadium likely has footage of whatever happened.

item.title: SB Nation Reacts: Arizona football fans pick their preferred bowl slot
item.description: San Diego, California - January 02: Arizona and SMU players run over the Holiday Bowl logo during the Holiday Bowl at Snapdragon Stadium on Friday, Jan. 2, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Meg McLaughlin / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images) Arizona will be playing in a bowl game next month, marking the first time since 2012-15 it gets to go bowling in consecutive season. The Wildcats have been bowl eligible in three of the last four years. But which bowl game will the UA play in? Despite being in the Big 12 Conference since 2014, Arizona is still considered a so-called “Pac-12 legacy school” when it comes to bowl affiliations. This is the last year of this connection, meaning after the 2027 season the Wildcats will be able to play in a whole different set of bowls (assuming they’re still around with the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams). We asked our readers which of the most likely bowl destinations they think Arizona will end up, and a plurality are expecting a repeat of last season. Arizona lost 24-19 to SMU at the Holiday Bowl in January, a game it trailed 24-0 before making a late push for the comeback. It was the UA’s first appearance in the San Diego-based game since 2009. Holiday is the third in the pecking order for bowl selections among Pac-12 legacy teams, with the Alamo Bowl getting first pick and then Las Vegas. The Sun Bowl is fourth, followed by the Poinsettia Bowl and Independence Bowl. Arizona beat Oklahoma in the 2023 Alamo Bowl but hasn’t been in the Vegas or Sun bowls in a long time. The last appearance in Sin City for a bowl game was in 2008, a 31-21 win over BYU, and the last trip to El Paso for the Sun Bowl resulted in a 20-15 loss to Baylor in 1992. Arizona is one of seven Pac-12 legacy schools that are currently bowl-eligible, while Oregon State and Stanford are each a win away from six. UCLA and Utah are virtual locks for the College Football Playoff, taking them out of the mix, while Oregon and USC could also sneak into the 12-team field. If not, those squads would be likely be the first choices for bowls ahead of Arizona.

item.title: 2026 D-backs Off-season questions, #3: Trading Ketel Marte, or not?
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CA - SEPTEMBER 25: Ketel Marte #4 of the Arizona Diamondbacks warms up during the game between the Arizona Diamondbacks and the San Diego Padres at Petco Park on Friday, September 25, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Brendon Baranov/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images In his final game of 2026, Ketel Marte passed Luis Gonzalez as the all-time Diamondbacks leader for games played, appearing in his 1,195th regular season contest for Arizona. He is now ranked top three in most offensive counting stats, alongside Gonzalez and Paul Goldschmidt. There are still four seasons left on the contract extension which Marte signed in April 2025. But there is a very real possibility that Ketel has played his final game for the D-backs. Indications are that the team is now looking to trade him, the second baseman having apparently worn out his welcome in Arizona, barely eighteen months after signing that six-year extension. We recently discussed the rumors about a potential Marte trade. At the time of writing, the Baltimore Orioles and the Toronto Blue Jays are the teams who have been most frequently mentioned as a landing spot in any trade. Though with his long-term status on the Diamondbacks, Ketel now has the full ability to decline any move, a situation which complicates the process considerably. But will the team pull the trigger? And should they, especially if the return is not one they consider appropriate for a player of Marte’s undeniable talents. We are, after all, barely a year removed from Ketel winning the Silver Slugger and being mentioned on MVP ballots. However, Mrs. SnakePit would likely point to Marte’s performance since the contract extension as further evidence for her theory that giving large, long-term contact extensions to players is frequently a mistake. [She still hasn’t forgiven Eric Byrnes, and considers fellow Cuban Yasmany Tomas a disgrace to the entire nation] When he signed the deal, Marte was coming off a year where he finished third in the NL MVP voting, and deservedly so, since he put up 6.8 bWAR. But that is basically his total production over the two seasons since then, with a pair of sharp drops, first to 4.4 bWAR and then all the way down to 2.5 bWAR. That’s a troubling trend. One year might be a blip, but consecutive declines of around two wins is a concern. It’s also worth noting, Marte recently turned 33. At this point, we should be expecting a decline of about half a win per season, due to the aging curve. If you’re starting in the 6-7 win range, as Marte was when the six-year extension was signed, that’s bearable. He’d still be worth 3-4 WAR by the end of the contract. item.description: Inter Milan considering a move for struggling Arsenal star Cristhian Mosquera has become something of a forgotten man at Arsenal this season, with the club having a fully fit defensive group and signing Ezri Konsa in the summer . The competition for places has made it increasingly difficult for the young defender to secure regular playing time. When William Saliba was sidelined for several months , Mosquera was widely expected to step up and fill the void left by the Frenchman. However, things did not develop as anticipated, with another defender taking advantage of the opportunity. Konsa has proved to be a superb addition to the squad and has impressed since beginning his career with the Gunners. His performances have strengthened Arsenal’s defensive options and made competition for a starting position even tougher. Sport Witness reveals that Mosquera could now be considering his future, with reports from Italy linking him with a potential move to Serie A. Inter Milan are reportedly among the clubs monitoring his situation and are keen to explore the possibility of bringing him to their squad. Inter Milan interested in Arsenal defender The Italian club are said to be a huge admirer of Mosquera and believes he could represent an attractive opportunity in the transfer market. His limited involvement at Arsenal could make a move more realistic, particularly if the player decides that regular football is necessary for his development. item.title: 'Selectors are making a blunder': Krishnamachari Srikkanth questions India's handling of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
item.description: Former India captain and chief selector Krishnamachari Srikkanth has launched a strong criticism of the selectors and team management over their handling of teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, insisting that the youngster deserves a consistent run in the Indian side. Srikkanth believes the 15-year-old has the potential to become a match-winner across formats and even play a significant role in reviving Test cricket globally. Speaking at the sports event on Friday, Srikkanth said the selectors and team management were making a mistake by not providing Sooryavanshi with enough opportunities. 'They are discouraging him': Srikkanth slams selectors over Sooryavanshi's treatment Srikkanth questioned the decision to pick Sooryavanshi for one match and then leave him out for several games, stressing that the youngster needed sustained opportunities to prove his abilities. "What they (selectors and team management) are doing with him is not right. They are not encouraging him; they are discouraging him, which is not done. These guys are making a blunder. They play him for one match, they don't play him for five matches. That's not done. Sad," Srikkanth said at the event. 'Test cricket revival happens all over the world': Srikkanth backs Sooryavanshi's potential Going a step further, Srikkanth suggested that Sooryavanshi's success in the longest format could generate renewed interest in Test cricket, not just in India but across the cricketing world. "If Sooryavanshi clicks in Test cricket, a Test cricket revival happens all over the world, not just for India, all over the world. Today in New Zealand, when he was playing the T20 matches, people came all the way -- a full crowd -- to watch Sooryavanshi bat. Wherever he goes, everybody comes to watch Sooryavanshi bat," he said. He called on the selectors to show faith in the youngster and give him a sustained run instead of making frequent changes to his selection. "This boy has done so brilliantly for you -- let him play all the matches. Do you mean to say he is not good enough to play Test or One Day cricket? He is 100 per cent sure to play good One Day cricket. Give him 20 innings, tell him he won't get dropped -- you do whatever you want. That boy will win five to seven matches single-handedly for you. "And if he scores in Test cricket, the whole world will start reviving Test cricket everywhere, in any part of the world," he added.

item.title: ‘He’s done’ – Stephen A. Smith says there is no way back for Dallas Cowboys man who he simply cannot defend
item.description: Photo by Ben Liebenberg/Getty Images Stephen A. Smith says there is no way back for Christian Parker with the Dallas Cowboys even if they do improve. Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker has been stripped of his responsibility to call plays. The decision was made earlier in the week after the team’s 46-40 loss at home to the San Francisco 49ers. The Cowboys gave up almost 600 yards, with their defense now ranking dead last after 10 games. Parker’s responsibilities will be taken on by Mike Pettine, who was originally brought in as a consultant to help him out. Speaking to First Take, Stephen A. Smith says that even if the Cowboys do improve, there is no way that Parker will get his old role back. Smith said: “I’m not defending Christian Parker because it can’t be defended—I understand that. And I don’t think Mike Pettine is going to do a damn thing, personally, if they go ahead and make this change. “Well, my point is, let’s take the opposite approach, let’s take the Skip Bayless approach. What if Mike Pettine does right this ship? What if the Dallas Cowboys elevate to decent or respectable? What if that happens? “Well, then Christian Parker isn’t going to get his job back. “It’s not like you’re going to turn around and say, ‘OK, you can come back now that somebody else has corrected it.’ You aren’t going to do that. “So clearly, the bottom line is he’s done, any way you want to slice it.” Stephen A. Smith says Parker is now worse off The Cowboys hired Christian Parker after his two-year stint as the passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach on the Philadelphia Eagles. Smith argues that he is now in a worse position after his setback with the Cowboys: “He was an assistant to Vic Fangio in Philadelphia, a disciple of his. Now you’re going to be one to Mike Pettine? “I’m sorry, that’s a downgrade as far as I’m concerned.” Smith adds that while Parker cannot be defended, he believes the players must take their share of the blame. “I just needed to take a moment to point the finger at the players. You’ve got this cat right now, 34 years old, ‘boy wonder’ supposedly, essentially demoted right in front of y’all’s faces as players. Missed tackles. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images This weekend, the Buffalo Bills square off against one of the franchise’s biggest foes, historically. In fact, some would say the Miami Dolphins are still Buffalo’s biggest rival. True or otherwise, to call Bills-Dolphins a heated rivalry at this juncture is doing more lip service to the past than the present. What is a fact is that Buffalo and Miami have alternated between lengthy spans of one-sided win streaks. Since the end of the 1980s, the Bills have largely had the Dolphins’ number. Sunday’s game at Highmark Stadium marks the 17th regular-season game for quarterback Josh Allen against Miami, a series that’s seen some of his most dominant play. Since Allen took over as QB1 in 2018, Buffalo is 14-3 against the Dolphins (including 1 playoff win). In 16 regular-season games, Allen has thrown for 4,256 yards with 42 touchdowns and nine interceptions, adding 703 rushing yards and another nine touchdowns on the ground. Let that sink in a moment as you consider the sort of stat line often associated with NFL MVP-winning quarterbacks. Dolphins week belongs to Josh Allen, and the latest matchup isn’t likely to change the narrative regardless of his final stat line. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook agree, where the majority among more than 200 currently available wager options predict favorable outcomes for Allen . Clearly, people expect Allen to put up significant stats in Week 11. I believe Allen will have a strong game, perhaps running for a pair of touchdowns and throwing for a couple more scores. It’s his yardage where I’m hesitant to favor huge numbers. Allen’s again an MVP favorite for a reason, and the Dolphins are at a very different stage of team development compared to the Bills. At the same time, it’s important to remember that Buffalo is a run-first team under head coach Joe Brady, thanks to a mauling offensive line that features defending NFL rushing champion James Cook III. Through nine games, Cook is second in the league with 971 yards, and he’s set a goal to reach 2,000 yards on the ground this season. item.title: Cadillac Cancels Plan To Build Its Own V6 F1 Engine
item.description: General Motors is pumping the brakes on its Formula 1 engine timeline. Cadillac will push back the debut of its in-house F1 power unit by one full year, shifting from 2029 to 2030 so its factory engine program launches alongside Formula 1's newly proposed V8 regulations. Rather than dumping millions of dollars into building a complex V6 hybrid for a single lame-duck season, the American team will extend its customer engine partnership with Ferrari through the end of 2029. Originally, GM planned to transition Cadillac from a Ferrari customer outfit into a full-fledged works team in 2029, operating under the assumption that the current 1.6-liter V6 hybrid cycle would run through 2030 before new rules arrived in 2031. Related Video That timeline accelerated ahead of this week's Las Vegas Grand Prix. Formula 1, the FIA, and existing engine manufacturers reached an agreement in principle to cut the current engine cycle short and introduce the 2.1-liter turbocharged V8s with scaled-back hybrid assistance starting in 2030. The paperwork still awaits final sign-off from the FIA World Motor Sport Council next month, McLaren CEO Zak Brown confirmed it was happening during Thursday's team principals' press conference. "Yes, we would remain a customer of Ferrari through 2029 and bring the Cadillac power unit online in 2030 with the V8," Cadillac F1 CEO Dan Towriss told Motorsport.com in Las Vegas. "I think we're glad to see the series really coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030," Towriss said. "We're super happy with that." Why not? General Motors has a rich history of building race-winning V8 engines, from muscle cars to sports cars to IndyCars. Work back in the States is ramping up fast. General Motors will officially open its dedicated F1 power unit headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, on December 18. Once the doors open, engineers will temporarily run parallel development programs-using their existing V6 groundwork as a baseline while pivoting primary design efforts toward the 2030 V8. "Well, for a period of time, we're working on both," Towriss explained. "So they've already got a V6 base to build off of and then we're working towards the V8. There are a number of designs that are in motion now, so there's a lot of good foundation for what we're trying to build and the direction we're headed in." Of course, there are questions about the team's future after news broke that Mark Walter is reportedly exploring a sale of TWG's stake in Cadillac Formula 1 amid the ongoing DOJ and SEC investigation into the holding company. With an asking price of no less than $3 billion, there are rumored to be at least seven interested parties. Will Cadillac F1 survive until GM's engine is ready? Become an AutoGuide insider. item.title: Formula 1’s Obsession With Spectacle Always Led It To Las Vegas
item.description: F1 always intended to host a Grand Prix on the Las Vegas Strip, but it wouldn't come to fruition until 2023. (Photo credit: Mark Thompson, Getty Images/Red Bull Content Pool) Formula 1 has always had an appetite for spectacle. The Las Vegas Grand Prix has perfectly embodied that vision, as its earlier iteration, the Caesars Palace Grand Prix , remains a painful reminder of its pitfalls. Together they have marked important turning points for the future of the championship. Caesars Palace Grand Prix: F1's first foray into spectacle The Caesars Palace Grand Prix circuit was a relatively featureless track built in a casino parking lot. (Photo: Yoyodu10 via Wikimedia Commons) The first three decades of Formula 1 looked dramatically different from the sport we know today, in large part because it remained a fairly amateur affair. Grands Prix taking place in major city centers used to be a rarity. For the United States, that was evident when the sport came to compete at Watkins Glen International. Located in a sleepy hamlet in upstate New York, Watkins Glen was F1's first true American home, hosting the United States Grand Prix from 1961 to 1980. The track is nowhere near any major hub for air or sea travel, the town of Watkins Glen itself has rarely boasted more than 3,000 inhabitants since its founding in 1870, and the lodgings were as equally rudimentary as the track facilities. For a sport that in the 1960s was used to racing in the countryside of England, Belgium, and France, and that often failed to pay all but the top drivers a living wage, Watkins Glen was perfectly aligned with F1’s spirit. But the sport began to evolve in the 1970s. Advancements in technology resulted in quicker cars, while behind-the-scenes politics brought about an increase in prize purses and the introduction of television broadcast package sales. F1 thus began to reach wider audiences, and the men in charge of the sport wanted to present Formula 1 as the pinnacle of motor racing in every aspect. That meant transforming the calendar. In 1976, Formula 1 added a new race in Long Beach, California. Organizer Chris Pook felt he had an opportunity to tie the international glamour of F1 to the glamour of nearby Los Angeles in order to create an unforgettable event. And it worked: the race, called the United States Grand Prix West, attracted plenty of celebrity attention, and drivers enjoyed the technical circuit. Pook had shown The Powers That Be in Formula 1 that a street circuit in an eye-catching location could work. So, F1 turned its eyes to Las Vegas. The 1970s was a decade of transition for Formula 1, and the city of Las Vegas. Construction had slowed after much of the mafia money funding casinos had been ousted, but visitor numbers nevertheless almost doubled. Boxing had long been a favored Vegas spectacle, but when daredevil Evel Knievel was contracted to jump over the fountains in front of Caesars Palace in 1967, motorsport entered the conversation. Drake Maye's injury — and the lack of information made available relating to the injury — has left Patriots fans in the mire in recent days. The Patriots gunslinger, who was cut down in New England's loss to the Lions on Sunday, is expected to miss most of — it not all — of the rest of the season with his malady. It's unclear who will take his place as New England starter in his stead — Tommy DeVito seems the leading candidate, although things appear murky during the bye week. Maye's status has been dictated by whispers and murmurs, at least thus far. On Friday, we finally got some tangible news on the true nature of Maye's ailment — as well as what onlookers can expect of his return. Here's what you need to know. MORE: Bill Belichick's Hall Of Fame Situation Takes Another Unexpected Turn We Finally Know the Severity of Drake Maye's injury Maye was diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter. There was no ligament damage, leaving open the possibility that Maye could potentially return at some point in the season, although he's expected to be sidelined for much — if not all — of the remainder of the year. According to Reiss and Schefter, the nature of Maye's injury is such that he won't have to undergo surgery, In normal circumstances, he would be placed on injured reserve. New England's IR is incredibly bloated, however, so much so that the team has nearly reached its limit on number of players that can be designated to be placed on it. The Patriots are currently slated to start Tommy DeVito in Maye's absence. The team could dip into the free agent pool ahead of Week 12; there are a host of sidewinders who could get some buzz, including Daniel Jones and Jake Browning. New England (5-5) sits one game out a playoff berth. The Pats will take on the Bills, Vikings, Chiefs and Broncos as part of their end-of-season slate. No team has qualified as a wild-card team without winning at least nine games since the league extended the season to 17 games in 2021. item.description: Celtics' Loss To Nuggets Exposes A Problem Boston Cannot Ignore originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics had enough opportunities to leave Denver with a victory. Instead, a troubling stretch of offensive basketball helped turn a 17-point lead into a 105-101 defeat against the Nuggets on Wednesday night. Boston entered halftime ahead 61-49, but the Nuggets used a 20-4 third-quarter run to seize control. The Celtics went scoreless for 4:35 during that stretch, allowing Denver to erase the advantage and eventually move in front. For a team capable of producing explosive offensive stretches, the sudden inability to generate reliable points is particularly concerning. Boston's Three-Point Shooting Became A Major Liability The Celtics made only 11 of their 44 attempts from beyond the arc. That represented a dramatic departure from the team's 38.2% season shooting percentage entering the game. Celtics next 3 games: - Kings - Warriors (no Steph) - Wizards Absolutely need to win them all. — CelticsUnite (@CelticsUnite18) November 20, 2026 Missing perimeter shots is not automatically a sign of poor offense. Boston's larger problem was its inability to find enough alternative scoring opportunities when the outside shots stopped falling. Jayson Tatum finished with 24 points, but only four came after halftime. He also committed six turnovers, including four during Denver's third-quarter comeback. Payton Pritchard contributed 15 points, while Neemias Queta provided one of Boston's brighter performances with 17 points and 10 rebounds. MORE : Why Stephen Curry Won’t Play in Celtics vs. Warriors Game on Sunday Celtics Need Better Answers Late In Games The final 16 minutes featured 15 lead changes, demonstrating that Boston recovered sufficiently to remain competitive after its disastrous third-quarter stretch. Yet Denver made the decisive plays. DeMar DeRozan's free throws with 49 seconds remaining put the Nuggets ahead for good. The loss marked Boston's first consecutive regular-season defeats since March. One difficult road game should not define a season, but the details matter. Boston needs to manufacture quality possessions when its perimeter shooting disappears, especially against opponents capable of capitalizing on extended droughts. The Celtics have enough offensive talent to overcome an occasional difficult shooting night, but their execution must improve when games become close. item.title: Fantasy Football Impact: What Anthony Richardson Starting For The Colts Means For Jonathan Taylor And Tyler Warren
item.description: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. (5) throws the ball against the Houston Texans during the fourth quarter at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Indianapolis Colts have decided to turn to quarterback Anthony Richardson as their starter in Week 12 and presumably for the remainder of the season. This comes after the team didn't just bench Daniel Jones but outright cut him from the roster. This will almost surely be Richardson's last chance to show the Colts any reason to want to keep him around beyond this season. #Colts QB Anthony Richardson Sr. is the new starting QB. pic.twitter.com/iSKDsQaTVZ - Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 20, 2026 Fantasy Impact QB Anthony Richardson, Indianapolis Colts This is a big opportunity for Richardson. While we don't expect him to shock anyone and suddenly become an elite quarterback, we do expect him to be better than Daniel Jones and much better for the Colts' fantasy weapons. That's not to say that Richardson is a better quarterback than Jones, but he is more capable of making something out of nothing. Especially now, with Jones coming off serious leg injuries. If nothing else, Richardson is a freak athlete who can make plays and buy time with his legs. The supporting cast is barren, with the offensive line and WR corps significantly diminished from what it was expected to be at the start of the season. He at least has some hope of surviving behind that offensive line and can make plays without any truly viable wide receivers on the outside. RB Jonathan Taylor, Indianapolis Colts It looks like Taylor could step back into a bell-cow role with Seth McGowan injuring his hamstring on Thursday Night Football. However, that doesn't matter if he continues to have lines, as he did in Week 11, rushing 11 times for 21 yards. The addition of Richardson to the offense should at least give defenses something else to focus on. Even if Richardson isn't much of a passer, he can beat you with his legs if you don't give him the respect he deserves as a runner. RB Tyler Warren, Indianapolis Colts Any change is a good change at this point for Tyler Warren; nevertheless, we don't expect things to get much better for Warren with Richardson in there. Unfortunately, his talent might not be enough to overcome his situation this season. item.description: Colts Jones $ Daniel Jones’ time in Indianapolis has come to an end. The Colts released Jones on Friday and will start Anthony Richardson going forward just eight months after signing Jones to a two-year, $88 million contract in March. The ex-Giants quarterback started 11 games for Indianapolis this season and made $49.79 million , according to overthecap.com. Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) stands on the sideline during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans in Houston, Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. AP Photo/David J. Phillip The Colts inked him to the largest two-year contract in league history on the heels of a standout 2025 season in which he started 13 games and threw for 3,101 yards, 19 touchdowns and eight interceptions, showing signs that his Giants struggles were behind him. Less than a year later, Jones is in the midst of the worst season of his career. His 1.7 quarterback rating against the Dolphins in Week 10 is the worst for any starting quarterback this season. Ahead of their Thursday night divisional contest with the Texans, head coach Shane Steichen said the team would stick with Jones on the short week . Jones then went 12 of 27 for 144 yards and an interception in the 26-3 loss. He now hits waivers — where he’ll stay in limbo until Monday at 4 p.m. — with a career-low 58.4 completion percentage, with seven passing touchdowns to 13 interceptions. The only guarantees in place are in the case of an injury, which would pay $6.5 million of Jones’ base salary and a $4 million roster bonus, per NFL insider Mike Garafolo . Giants fans will recall a similar situation where Jones struggled shortly after signing a large contract. Big Blue gave Jones a four-year, $160 million extension in March 2023, months after the team’s playoff berth that ended in the NFC divisional round. After his 2023 season was cut short in Week 9 following a torn ACL, Jones was benched in the midst of a dismal 2024 season before being released that November. item.title: A.J. Brown to miss multiple weeks with hamstring injury, per report
item.description: The hits keep on coming for the New England Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. Wide receiver A.J. Brown, who joined the team in a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles in April, is expected to be sidelined “multiple weeks” due to the hamstring injury he suffered last Sunday against the Detroit Lions. Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter of ESPN were first to report the severity of the ailment. Brown will now have missed time due to injury on three different occasions this season. The 29-year-old previously suffered a high ankle sprain in the third quarter of New England’s season opener against the Seattle Seahawks, and was placed on injured reserve shortly thereafter. After sitting out four games, he made his return in Week 6 but only appeared in two games before missing time with a knee issue. He sat out the next two contests before making his comeback against the Lions. After just his second of the day, a 21-yarder in the third quarter, he exited with the aforementioned hamstring issue. Brown did not return to the contest and was ruled out a short time later, joining quarterback Drake Maye on a long list of Patriots who got hurt in the eventual 35-10 defeat. How much time Brown will ultimately miss remains to be seen. However, for the time being, he will not be able to add to his current stat-line: playing 160 total snaps over four games this season, he has caught 11 passes for 128 yards. The Patriots traded a 2028 first-round draft pick and a 2027 fourth-rounder to the Eagles to bring Brown aboard during the offseason.

For a franchise that spent nearly a quarter-century setting the standard in professional football, the possibility of another rejection would be extraordinary. Those achievements have not eliminated debate over his candidacy. The Patriots faced league penalties for the 2007 videotaping scandal and the 2015 football-inflation controversy, matters that remain part of the broader discussion surrounding the dynasty. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
